newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-BOLIVIA REACH COPA AMERICA SEMI-FINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOLIVIA REACH COPA AMERICA SEMI-FINALS.

text.p: Bolivia, with the advantage of playing at high altitude, beat Colombia 2-1 Saturday to reach the semi-finals of the Copa America.
Marco Etcheverry and Erwin Sanchez put the host nation in a commanding position with goals in the first 25 minutes of an entertaining game.

Herman Gaviria gave Colombia some hope by pulling back a goal in the second half, the first Bolivia have conceded in the tournament, but his team did not look as if they had the lungs to force an equaliser in the thin air.

The highlight of the game came midway through the second half when Bolivia's Julio Cesar Baldivieso hit the crossbar from near the halfway line after seeing Colombia goalkeeper Farid Mondragon off his line.
Colombia had played their final first round match at sea level less than 48 hours before Saturday's quarter-final, which was played at 3,600 metres above sea level.

The Colombians, who rested their best players for the World Cup qualifiers which follow the Copa America, arrived just a couple of hours before kick off in an attempt to reduce the effects of the altitude.
But they barely had time to catch their breath before Bolivia scored, Etcheverry chipping a delicate free kick over the Colombia wall from 20 metres in the third minute.

Colombia's goalkeeping difficulties were again exposed 20 minutes later when Erwin Sanchez scored with a rasping 35-metre drive which was badly misjudged by goalkeeper Farid Mondragon. The ball bounced in front of Mondragon and went under his arms into the net.
Mondragon lost his place to Miguel Calero after committing a series of blunders in recent games but regained it Saturday after Calero himself looked shaky in his two outings.
Mondragon partially made up for his blunder in the second half with two excellent saves.
Herman Gaviria reduced the deficit in the 61st minute when he broke through the Bolivia defence and neatly chipped the ball over the advancing Carlos Trucco.
But in the last half hour, a third Bolivian goal looked more likely than a Colombian equaliser.

Bolivia - 1-Carlos Trucco, 7-Sergio Castillo, 2-Juan Manuel Pena, 3-Marco Sandy, 5-Oscar Sanchez, 16-Luis Cristaldo, 6-Vladimir Soria, 21-Erwin Sanchez (9-Jaime Moreno), 22-Julio Cesar Baldivieso, 10-Marco Etcheverry, 20-Ramiro Castillo (8-Milton Melgar, 70).

Colombia - 1-Farid Mondragon, 4-Jose Santa, 2-Ivan Cordoba, 5-Jorge Bermudez, 16-Luis Moreno, 14-Herman Gaviria, 6-Wilmar Perez (22-Neider Morantes, 24), 13-Wilmer Cabrera, 20-Victor Pacheco, 9-Victor Hugo Aristizabal, 17-Hamilton Ricard (7-Luis Zuleta, 65).
